text: Tata Motors Commercial Vehicles is expected to post Q2FY27 revenue of roughly Rs 24,218.4 crore (+43.6% YoY) per JM Financial and Rs 24,638.1 crore (+45.4% YoY) per Motilal Oswal, with volume around 1,35,114–1,37,339 units and a 53.1% YoY rise in light commercial vehicles.
Tata Motors became India’s second‑largest passenger‑vehicle manufacturer in H1 FY27, dispatching over 3.9 lakh units (+43% YoY) and overtaking Mahindra, aided by a 59% surge in utility‑vehicle sales.

Tata Motors CV's Q2FY27 results are expected to show profit growth of up to 44% YoY, driven by a volume expansion of around 43% YoY. Brokerage forecasts project revenue to rise 43.6% YoY to Rs 24,218.4 crore (JM Financial) or 45.4% YoY to Rs 24,638.1 crore (MOFSL), with adjusted PAT growth estimates of 44.3% (JM) and 25.7% (MOFSL), while margins face pressure despite a net price hike of 2.5% since July. Expected domestic volumes are 1,35,114 units (up 42.7% YoY and 24.5% QoQ) per JM and 1,37,339 units (up 43% YoY and around 26.3% sequentially) per MOFSL, led by LCVs up 53.1% YoY, and MOFSL maintains a Neutral rating with a target price of Rs 422 versus the market price of Rs 415.
note: Forecasts are correctly attributed; PAT growth is not uniform across brokerages (44.3% JM versus 25.7% MOFSL).

text: Analysts diverge on profit growth, forecasting PAT up 44.3% (JM) versus 25.7% (MOFSL); margins are expected to stay under pressure from input‑cost inflation despite a 2.5% price hike.

Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Stellantis have expanded their partnership to jointly develop vehicles using Tata’s architecture and technology, targeting more than 50 global markets with production in the FIAPL 50:50 joint venture in Pune.
The combined Iveco commercial‑vehicle business is projected to generate annual revenue of about €21 billion and sell over 590,000 vehicles.
note: The figures refer to the combined Tata Motors–Iveco business following the acquisition, not Iveco alone.

text: Tata Motors' €3.9 billion acquisition of Iveco has progressed as shareholders approved the tender offer, lowering the minimum acceptance threshold to 80 % and raising the offer price to €14.40 per share; the tender period runs from September 7 to October 26, 2026, and the deal remains contingent on securing the remaining silent shareholders to meet the 80 % threshold.
note: Shareholders approved the resolutions reducing the acceptance threshold to 80%; Tata Motors, not the shareholders, raised the offer price to €14.40.

text: The reduction of the acceptance threshold to 80% for the Iveco acquisition aligns with broader M&A trends where lower thresholds facilitate cross‑border consolidations in the commercial‑vehicle industry.
note: The evidence confirms the threshold reduction in this transaction but does not establish a broader M&A trend linking lower acceptance thresholds to cross-border commercial-vehicle consolidation.

text: The collaboration builds on a February 2026 MoU and aims to leverage India’s engineering expertise and manufacturing capacity to support export plans and strengthen India’s role in the global automotive production network.

Tata Motors’ €3.91‑billion bid for Iveco is in its final phase with a “best and final” offer of €14.40 per share and no further increases. Exor, Iveco’s largest shareholder, has committed its 27.06% stake, while minority holders (Davidson Kempner, Syquant Capital, Petrus Advisers) hold about 20% and have not tendered. The deal could succeed if the acceptance threshold falls to 80% after an upcoming shareholder vote; otherwise, a failed transaction would impact Iveco more severely than Tata Motors.
note: The cited article establishes minority holders' approximately 20% stake and their potential influence on acceptance, but does not confirm that they had not tendered their shares.

text: Two hedge funds and an activist investor hold ~20.4% of Iveco and could earn about €63 million at the €14.40 offer, plus €288 million extraordinary dividends. As of 21 Oct, only 33.4% of Iveco shares have been tendered; the offer closes on 26 Oct, making their participation critical for Tata to hit the 80% threshold.
note: The €63m represents a potential gain at the offer price; the €288m extraordinary dividends had already been received in April and are not future earnings from the tender.

text: Tata Motors overtook Mahindra & Mahindra to become India's second‑largest passenger‑vehicle maker in the April‑September 2026 period, with dispatches surging 43 % to over 3.9 lakh units, driven by a 59 % surge in utility‑vehicle dispatches.

Exor, holding 27.06% of Iveco’s common shares (43% of voting rights), has committed its stake, while minority shareholders Davidson Kempner, Syquant Capital and Petrus Advisers together hold about 20‑20.4% and have not tendered, creating risk to reaching the required acceptance threshold.
note: The sources distinguish Exor's 27.06% shareholding from its 43% voting rights; minority holdings are reported at approximately 20–20.4%.

text: Analysts preview Tata Motors CV Q2 FY27, expecting volume growth of around 43% YoY (≈1,35,114 units) and revenue growth of 44‑45% YoY to Rs 24,218.4‑24,638.1 crore. Profit growth estimates diverge (44.3% vs 25.7%). Margins under pressure due to input‑cost inflation; pricing hike of 2.5% since July.

Iveco Group shareholders approved all resolutions related to Tata Motors’ €3.91 billion acquisition, lowering the minimum acceptance threshold from 95% to 80%. The offer price was raised to €14.40 per share. Approved changes include conversion to a private limited company, a post‑offer demerger, and appointment of new board members. The tender offer is scheduled to close on 26 Oct, subject to remaining conditions.
